current.text: He re-signed with Atlanta on a 1-year, 21 million USD deal.
He is a projected starter next to Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu. Lloyd projects each starter for 30-plus minutes.
Lu Dort is the main threat to his starting spot. If Dort starts, it would most likely be in place of McCollum.
The experts disagree on his starting job. Lloyd and one other expert expect him to start over Dort. The newest note says he could come off the bench.
In Atlanta he has the ball more than anyone else on the team and has played point guard. The team has no true point guard. He shares ball handling with Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels.
After joining Atlanta he ranked 63rd for the rest of last season. Over the last two months he was top 70 while playing under 30 minutes.
Atlanta's strong finish last season was helped by an easy schedule.
Lloyd expects him to be better this season as a locked-in starter on a team pushing for the playoffs. Josh is also high on him.

The experts call his market price too low. His ADP sits around 100 to 117 across sites. Lloyd targets him around picks 80 to 90. Others like him as a last starter or bench pick. Josh paid 8 USD for him in an auction mock.
One expert would not draft him as high as his post-deadline rank because of his age.
Draft him to add points, threes and assists at guard. One expert has no worries about him being traded.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks. The team has 14 back-to-backs. Resting healthy players is not a concern, and the team did not shut players down last season.
Atlanta is projected for about 46 wins, somewhere between fourth and eighth in the East.

durable.text: He is a score-first guard, not a pure point guard.
He is an inconsistent free throw shooter and does not add much in steals or blocks.
Quin Snyder runs an egalitarian, high-movement offense that wants many threes and five-out spacing.

note: McCollum is a cheap guard: Yahoo values him at 3 USD and ESPN at 4 USD, and he went for 2 USD in our auction last season. The experts call his rank of about 100 to 117 too low after he finished last season at a top-70 pace in Atlanta, so plan to bid 3 to 6 USD for a last guard or bench spot and stop around 8 USD. His threes (about 2.5 per game) and points help most builds, but he adds little in FT%, rebounds and steals. In the first weeks, check that he starts over Lu Dort and keeps about 30 minutes.
